thread:
Sam L: Heads-up — after the 4823 merge we’re seeing a consistent latency delta on small-seq workloads in the canary. p50 up ~6% and p95 up ~9% for seq<=16 tests.
Maya R: ugh. which change in 4823 was the culprit? kernel selection heuristics or batching default?
Sam L: kernel selection path changed (prefer fused-mha when seq<32) + a batching heuristic tweak that groups smaller requests more aggressively. either could be it.
Alex C: can we bisect? I ran a quick git-bisect locally and it pointed at 8a9f3d7 (the kernel selection refactor) but noisy.
Sam L: did a CI bisect on dedicated infra too. here's the trimmed output:
```
$ git bisect start -- bad good
8a9f3d7 is the first bad commit
commit 8a9f3d7
Author: Alex C <alex@redwood>
Date:   2026-03-09
    runtime: kernel select refactor + fused-mha preference
```
Maya R: interesting. Alex, that refactor also touched kv-cache warmup ordering, right?
Alex C: yeah, reordered kernel decision before kv-warmup hint. thought it was innocuous but might change prefetch timing.
Priya S: perf-bot just flagged the canary job and held the rollout.
perf-bot: Canary perf gate FAILED: small-seq p50 delta 6.1% (threshold 5.0%). Holding rollout and notifying eng-runtime.
Sam L: canary hold is expected. we should figure root cause before reverting.Trying to reproduce with perf harness with flags toggled.
Maya R: can you paste the perf profile flame for seq=8? quick grep is fine.
Sam L: copied relevant lines — flame simplified:
```
flamegraph (seq=8):
  40% kernel_select::choose_fused_mha
  28% kv_cache::lookup (misses on first token)
  12% attention::dispatch
  20% other
```
Alex C: that stack suggests kernel selection is stealing cycles and causing kv-cache lookups to get delayed/warmed later -> higher first-token cost.
Priya S: so root cause is interplay between kernel selection and kv-cache warmup ordering. two approaches:
- revert refactor to restore previous warmup timing
- adjust kernel selection to be cheaper (fast path) for tiny sequences
- change perf tests / canary thresholds while we fix
Maya R: also note CI perf noise on runner-3 last night. some of these deltas are near noise floor.
Sam L: I ran microbench 50 runs vs 500 runs. 50-run median matches canary (bad). 500-run median shows delta down to 3.2%.
Priya S: that implies our perf-gate sampling is too small for high-variance microbench workloads. we should tighten harness not loosen gates.
Alex C: actionable plan I propose:
1) immediate: add a targeted microbench for seq<=16 that runs 200 samples and uses bootstrap CI for median CI; update perf-bot to use that for gate checks.
2) short-term patch: add a lightweight fast-path in kernel select for seq<=8 that returns previous selection quickly (no over-inspection).
3) tests: add an explicit kv-warmup unit test and instrument warmup ordering in the runtime (metric: kv_warmup_latency_ms)
4) if patch not ready in 24h, revert 8a9f3d7 for canary rollback.
Maya R: sounds good. for 1) I can add microbench harness changes and bump sample count. I also want to reduce noise by pinning CPU frequency governor in CI containers for these benches.
Sam L: added a temp flag --pin-cpu-freq to the bench harness. will run on canary nodes.
perf-bot: Added job: microbench-smallseq-v2 (200 samples) -> will run on canary pool.
Priya S: for 2) Alex, can you open a minimal PR that implements the fast-path + unit test? we want something small we can ship quickly.
Alex C: on it. PR up in ~2h. will include perf numbers vs master locally.
Sam L: results after enabling pin-cpu-freq + 200-sample bench:
```
before: p50 +6.1%
after:  p50 +1.9% (CI median @ 95% bootstrap)
```
Maya R: good sign — this confirms sampling and harness were amplifying the signal.
Priya S: still worth shipping the kernel fast-path since it reduces first-token latency in prod paths.
Sam L: agreed. I'll hold canary for now, but not revert yet. once Alex's PR lands and perf-bot shows green on microbench-smallseq-v2 we can unhold.
Alex C: PR created: #4891 — "fast-path kernel select for tiny sequences + kv-warmup metric". bench numbers attached.
perf-bot: PR #4891 triggered microbench-smallseq-v2 -> run queued.
deploy-bot: canary remains on hold until perf gates pass.
Sam L: okay next steps: Maya will update harness + pinning; Alex will push small patch; Priya will add kv_warmup_latency metric to telemetry and a unit test; I will monitor canary and rerun larger 500-sample bench overnight. update threads in #eng-runtime once the microbench result lands.
Maya R: will also add a note to eng-runtime runbook about sample sizes and noise thresholds.
Priya S: and we should add a flakiness detector to perf-bot that suggests increasing sample count automatically when variance > X.
Sam L: nice. thanks everyone. marking follow-ups: [Maya: harness change], [Alex: PR #4891], [Priya: telemetry/test], [Sam: overnight 500-run sweep].
Maya R: :thumbsup:
Alex C: :shipit:
Priya S: keeping canary held until PR green and microbench shows <=3% p50 delta.
Sam L: congrats on catching this before wide rollout. we'll retro next week to discuss kernel refactor review checklist and perf-gate tightening.
